subject: Tranche-based capacity escrow & burst clauses (MAP + pricing)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@octaveai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tranche-based capacity escrow & burst clauses (MAP + pricing)

Alan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, I put together a short mutual action plan (attached) that aligns the evaluation milestones with the commercial terms so we can move to a Dedicated reservation efficiently. High level:

- Eval phase: 2 weeks (technical POC + perf targets)
- Milestone 1 (end of week 2): 10-node GPU pool (baseline perf) -> invoice credit applied
- Milestone 2 (week 6): ramp to 50-GPU equivalent pool -> commit triggers pricing tier 2
- Term: target 12 months from go-live; optional 24-month upsell discount if committed by M2
- Burst: allowed up to 2x sustained for short windows; burst fee schedule attached

I've attached: Octave_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP + timeline) and redwood_dedicated_terms.pdf (standard reservation terms with our recommended burst clause and escrow options). Key asks from our side: sign-off on the MAP milestones so we can lock the pool sizing and start procurement for the tranche.

Two points I flagged for your team to confirm:
1) Acceptance criteria for Milestone 1 (latency at p95 and throughput target) so we can automate rollout.
2) Whether you prefer an operational (service-level) escrow for burst capacity vs. a monetary escrow. We typically use a capacity-escrow approach (ability to burst guaranteed via reserved slot escrow) but can be flexible.

If you prefer, Ben from pricing is on copy and can send a tranche-level pricing spreadsheet after we agree the MAP. Next steps: review the MAP and terms, come back with any redlines by EOD Tuesday so we can target a signature by next week.

Best,

—Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0137

Attachments: Octave_MAP_v2.xlsx, redwood_dedicated_terms.pdf

From: Alan Cho <alan.cho@octaveai.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@octaveai.com>
Date: 2027-08-11T11:04:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Tranche-based capacity escrow & burst clauses (MAP + pricing)

Stephanie —

Thanks for this and for walking us through the flow. The MAP is a good starting point. A few clarifying items from our ops and procurement team:

- Burst triggers: can you confirm what constitutes a \"burst window\" (rolling 5m average, or 15m peaks)? We need clear SLAs for when pricing switches to burst tier.
- Overage cap: can we put a monthly cap on burst fees for the first quarter while we calibrate our usage patterns?
- Term: our legal is pushing for a 9-month initial term with an auto-extension clause rather than locked 12 months. Is there flexibility on the economics (discounts/credits) if we shorten initial term?
- Quantized profile: we intend to evaluate a quantized LLM profile that reduces memory but increases micro-batch load. Could you provide the pricing delta for a quantized execution profile vs. baseline?

I've cc'd procurement; they'll want the pricing spreadsheet and a short summary of burst billing mechanics. If you can draft the capped-burst option (e.g., 2x allowed, capped extra fee of $X for Q1) that would be very helpful.

Appreciate it — can we aim to finalize the MAP and economics by next Friday (20th)?

—Alan Cho
Head of AI Ops, Octave AI
alan.cho@octaveai.com

Subject: RE: Tranche-based capacity escrow & burst clauses (MAP + pricing)

Team — quick thoughts after reviewing Alan's asks:

1) Burst window definition: agree to a rolling 15m peak for trigger, but offer a promotional cap for Q1. Proposal: 2.5x burst allowance for the first 90 days, with a monthly cap on burst fees set to 20% of committed spend for that month.
2) Term flexibility: we can accept a 9-month initial term if Octave increases the month-1 commit (or prepays a portion) OR if they agree to a 12-month true-up option once M2 is achieved.
3) Quantized pricing delta: Ben, please model a -12% per-token rate for quantized execution at our recommended quantization profile (INT8) vs baseline.

Operationally: prefer capacity-escrow (slot-reservation) rather than cash escrow; it gives them guaranteed burstability without holding funds. Legal can scope the escrow SLA.

Ben — can you push a revised tranche pricing workbook with the capped-burst scenario and the 9-month/12-month economics? Include a DocuSign-ready MSA addendum.

—Laura
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Updated tranche pricing + capped burst option

Alan —

Attached is a refreshed pricing workbook (20270813_Octave_pricing_tranches.xlsx) and a short summary below. I also uploaded a DocuSign envelope for the MAP/terms (link included).

Summary highlights (numbers are illustrative):
- Baseline: 50-GPU equivalent pool (v100-eq) / 12-month list $178k/mo -> Tier 2 discounted $150k/mo on signed 12-mo commit.
- 9-month initial: equivalent monthly at $165k/mo + 6% one-time setup offset (or optional prepay to reduce to $158k/mo).
- Quantized (INT8): -12% on token rates; recommended for eval if latency-sensitive.
- Burst: 2.5x allowed for first 90 days; burst fee is $0.12/token-equivalent above committed capacity, monthly cap at 20% of committed spend for Q1. After Q1 burst allowance reverts to 2.0x with standard burst fees.

Attachments: 20270813_Octave_pricing_tranches.xlsx
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/doc/ABC-987654321

If those numbers look reasonable, we can route the MSA addendum to procurement and legal. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk the workbook.

Cheers,
